historical_references.context: Radhi bin Abi-Hafs al-Akhtab was a distinguished scholar of Islamic jurisprudence and tradition during the early Islamic period. He was born in Kufa and studied under some of the most renowned scholars of his time, including Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq and Abdullah ibn Mubarak. Radhi's scholarly contributions included the compilation of the 'Musnad of Radhi', which is considered one of the earliest collections of Hadith (sayings and actions of the Prophet Muhammad). He is also known for his commentary on the Sahih of Bukhari and his work on Islamic inheritance law.

historical_references.context: Radhi al-Din Mohammad ibn Timur, also known as Timur the Lame or Tamerlane, was a Central Asian conqueror and founder of the Timurid Empire. He was born in Shahr-i-Sabz in present-day Uzbekistan and rose to power through military campaigns that expanded his empire from Mongolia to the Mediterranean Sea. Radhi al-Din is known for his military conquests and his patronage of art, architecture, and literature. He was particularly interested in Islamic scholarship and supported many scholars and institutions, including the Observatory in Samarkand and the Madrasa-i-Sultani in Herat. Radhi al-Din is also known for his promotion of the Islamic faith, particularly the Hanafi school of jurisprudence, which was the dominant school in his empire.
